slides.narration: Chapter 17: The Lepton Masses. The electron, muon, and tau — the three charged leptons — satisfy a remarkable relation that has puzzled physicists for decades. The tower explains why.

The Koide relation says: take the square roots of the three lepton masses, add them, square the sum, and divide by the sum of the masses themselves. The result is exactly two-thirds — to six parts per million. The framework explains why: the tower's stage structure forces this ratio.
